Emma — following up with the technical inventory and clarifications below. Sorry for the slightly long note, wanted to make the mapping explicit for your legal/security team.

1) Evidence inventory (what we can provide and ETA)
- SOC 2 Type II summary statement (control areas relevant to cross-border transfers): available; ETA for extract & summary: 2028-03-08.
- Subprocessor registry (names + processing region + contract start): export-ready CSV; ETA: 2028-03-07. Note: for sensitivity reasons we provide location-region (EU/US/APAC) rather than precise datacenter addresses.
- Audit logs outline (what logs we retain, retention windows, and access process): one-page doc; ETA: 2028-03-07.
- KM KMS/HSM architecture note (how keys are managed in private deployments): one-page; ETA: 2028-03-09.

2) TIA vs SCCs: technical position
- Our serving runtime can be routed to EU-only capacity. If Clinicware requires contract-level guarantees that traffic will not leave EU regions, a TIA is appropriate because it documents the operational controls and routing commitments.
- If you can accept SCCs with the exhibit noting EU-only routing as a best-effort (and fallback to nearby region under capacity events), then we can remain with SCCs-only and close faster.

3) Escalation / exception path (if TIA required)
- Step 1: Technical review (Redwood infra & Clinicware infra) — 3 business days.
- Step 2: Security sign-off and written TIA draft — 5 business days.
- Step 3: Executive approval (if modifications to standard SLA/rollout) — up to 7 business days.

Given Clinicware's two-week timeline, the fastest path is SCCs-only with the EU-routing exhibit and the evidence inventory provided by 2028-03-09. If Clinicware insists on a binding TIA, we'll need to start the escalation today to hit your timeline.

Attachments: TransferImpact-Evidence-Inventory.xlsx (finalized), SCCs_Exhibit_v3.docx (annotated)

Happy to jump on a short call today if that helps move decisions faster.
